# HANDOFF — cal.diy (personal ledger, untracked)

**What is true.** Read first, every session. Append-only in the step log; standing sections
edited in place when they go stale. Process: `docs/AGENT-PRACTICES.md`. What is next:
`PASSOFF.md`.

Started 2026-09-14. Nothing below is committed or visible to anyone else.

---

## Orientation

`CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy` is a course-org fork of Cal.com — a Yarn 4 / Turbo monorepo (Next.js web
app, NestJS API v2, Postgres + Prisma, tRPC). The repo's conventions are upstream Cal.com's and
are **not ours to set**; see `docs/AGENT-PRACTICES.md` §Posture.

Owner: Zach. **Interactive — ask in chat, in the same turn, batched, when a decision is his.**

Read first, in order:
1. `CONTRIBUTING.md` — house rules, approval-before-feature-work, PR size limits.
2. `AGENTS.md` (`CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to it) — code conventions.
3. The `agents/rules/*.md` files matching what you are touching.
4. `docs/AGENT-PRACTICES.md` — the process standard.
5. This file, then `PASSOFF.md`.

---

## Environment

**Verified 2026-09-14 in the primary checkout (`~/Projects/cal.diy`, branch `short`).**

> ⚠️ **Node 26 does not work here. Use Node 22.14.0.** On Node 26.7.0 `yarn prisma generate`
> exits 1: the zod generator calls `fs.rmdir(..., {recursive: true})`, removed in modern Node —
> `Error while deleting old data in path packages/prisma/zod: The property 'options.recursive'
> is no longer supported. Received true`. Prisma Client (6.16.1), the Kysely types and the enum
> generator all succeed; only the zod step fails, and it takes the command's exit code with it.
> Note the docs disagree: `students.md` says Node v24.x (verified 2026-07-16), `AGENTS.md` says
> nothing, and `package.json` `engines` pins only npm and yarn — **never Node**. 22.14.0 is the
> version verified to run every gate here.

| Fact | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Node — **use this** | **v22.14.0**, at `/opt/homebrew/opt/node@22/bin` — not on PATH by default | verified 2026-09-14: every gate below ran on it |
| Node — default on PATH | v26.7.0 (`/opt/homebrew/bin/node`) — **breaks `prisma generate`** | verified 2026-09-14 |
| `node@24`, `node@25` | do **not** exist; they are alias symlinks to the single `node` keg (26.7.0) | `ls -ld /opt/homebrew/opt/node@24` |
| Package manager | yarn **4.12.0**, vendored in-repo at `.yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs` | `.yarnrc.yml` `yarnPath` |
| corepack | not on PATH by default; `npm i -g corepack && corepack enable` fixes it | verified 2026-09-14 |
| Database | **PostgreSQL 14.18 via Homebrew, running as a brew service on port 5432** — not Docker, which is not installed. `students.md` assumes Docker for Postgres + Mailhog; this is a documented local deviation. Database `calendso`, owner `zachshort` (superuser) | set up + verified 2026-09-14 |
| `.env` DB URLs | changed from the `.env.example` default `postgres:@localhost:5450` to **`postgresql://zachshort@localhost:5432/calendso`** to match the native install | verified 2026-09-14 |
| Mailhog | **not running** (it is the other half of the Docker compose). Anything that sends mail locally will have nowhere to deliver | 2026-09-14 |
| Default branch | `main` | `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` |
| Prisma migrations | 595 + `migration_lock.toml`, timestamped `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_name` | `ls packages/prisma/migrations` |
| `yarn install` | exit 0 in **1m12s**, producing **3.4G** of `node_modules` | verified 2026-09-14 |

**Setup, on any fresh checkout or worktree** (rationale: `docs/AGENT-PRACTICES.md` Part 6):

```bash
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/node@22/bin:$PATH"   # FIRST. Node 26 breaks prisma generate.
node --version              # must print v22.14.0
yarn --version              # must print 4.12.0
yarn
cp .env.example .env        # then NEXTAUTH_SECRET + CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY (students.md)
yarn prisma generate        # must exit 0; on Node 26 it will not
yarn type-check:ci --force  # paste the output — do not assert "setup done"
```

Measured with a database present; before the DB existed the same tree reported **406** files with identical test counts, so one file's collection depends on the DB |

> 2026-09-14 printed `Tasks: 11 successful ... Cached: 11 cached, 11 total >>> FULL TURBO` —
> it executed nothing. `type-check:ci` is prescribed with `--force` for exactly this reason
> (`AGENTS.md`) and lint is not, which makes lint the easier of the two to fool. **Use
> `yarn lint --force` when the number matters.**

**What an agent cannot do here.** No CI can be triggered from a session — `pr.yml` gates every
job behind trust plus the `run-ci` / `ready-for-e2e` labels, which only a maintainer sets. With
no Docker there is no local Postgres, so DB-backed tests and `yarn db-seed` cannot run, and no
page can be seen rendered. Anything needing a human to look at a screen goes in the hand-back as
an explicit "do this, expect that", and the session waits.

### Settled: how AI logs are captured (D4)

Syllabus §16: "An AI log is the record of an AI conversation with an AI tool — the prompts,
responses, and tool used. Logs are pushed to the team's GitHub repository rather than submitted
separately, and **referenced from the related GitHub issue**." Separately, "for each issue or
sprint, include a short written rationale (in the pull request description or sprint report)
explaining how AI output was used, especially when a suggestion was modified or rejected."
So the log is the **transcript**; the rationale is a different artifact and lives in the PR/report.

**The authoritative spec is <https://csci-435-se.github.io/ai-logs/>** (read 2026-09-14) — not
`ai-logs/README.md`, which only summarises it and links a `docs/sprints.md` that exists on no
ref. Requirements, verbatim where it matters:

- Path `ai-logs/sprint<N>/<github-username>/`; filename `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`.
  Zach's GitHub login is **`zach-short`** (confirmed via `gh api user`). Tool id for this tool
  is **`claude-code`**; `claude-desktop` is the separate Claude Desktop chat app.
- The log must state **the model/tool used** ("e.g. 'Claude Sonnet 4.5 via Claude Code'"), carry
  **the full prompt and response history**, and for agentic tools **all file edits and commands
  run**. A log with "only your prompts (no AI responses), or that is clearly incomplete" does
  **not** meet the requirement. SpecStory satisfies all three: every agent turn is headed
  `_**Agent (claude-opus-5 <timestamp>)**_`, so the model is stated throughout.
- **Files pasted into a session as context** (images, PDFs, snippets) go in a folder beside the
  log with the same name minus `.md`. Report evidence such as D1 screenshots is *not* session
  context and does not belong there.
- **Each log is referenced from the related GitHub issue** as a comment, one per contributor:

  ```
  | # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
  ```

  with a link to the log file and the contributor's role (Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other). "No AI used." if none. **This is the "link" — it points at the log file,
  and it lives in an issue comment, not inside the log.**
- **At sprint end, run `specstory sync` once more** and copy the sprint's files across; a sync
  is only a snapshot of the session so far.

**SpecStory is installed** (`~/.local/bin/specstory`, v2.10.0) and — importantly — **sessions
that were never launched via `specstory run` can still be recovered**, which the course warns is
otherwise hard after the fact:

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
specstory list claude                                  # sessions for THIS directory
specstory sync -s <session-id> --output-dir <dir> --local-time-zone
```

Two gotchas, both verified 2026-09-14:

- **Sessions are bucketed by the directory the session ran in.** A session run inside
  `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` is **not** listed from the repo root — run `specstory list` from
  the same directory the session used, or it looks like the log does not exist.
- **A sync is a snapshot.** Re-run it at the end of a session, or the log stops partway.

**Before committing any transcript, scan it for secrets (R16).** SpecStory redacts by default,
but verify rather than trust: grep the file for the literal values in `.env` and for key shapes
(`ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}`, `AKIA`, `BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY`). Done for the
2026-09-14 log: zero hits.

## Invariants — how things work; do not break these

Each cites the repo rule that owns it. Break one and it still compiles.

- **`select`, never `include`, in Prisma queries; `credential.key` never leaves a query** —
  `agents/rules/data-prefer-select-over-include.md`, `AGENTS.md`.
- **No business logic in repositories; no Prisma outside them** —
  `agents/rules/data-repository-pattern.md`.
- **Package layering is acyclic**: `lib` → `app-store` → `features` → `trpc` → `apps/web` —
  `agents/rules/architecture-circular-dependencies.md`.
- **`packages/features/**` must not import `@calcom/trpc`** —
  `agents/rules/architecture-features-modules.md`.
- **`apps/api/v2` imports features/trpc only via `@calcom/platform-libraries`** — `AGENTS.md`.
- **Permission checks in `page.tsx`, never `layout.tsx`** — `AGENTS.md`.
- **Never edit `*.generated.ts`** — `agents/rules/patterns-app-store.md`.
- **No breaking changes to v1/v2 endpoints; version instead** —
  `agents/rules/api-no-breaking-changes.md`.
- **All UI strings via `t()` and `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`** — `AGENTS.md`.

## Known API facts and quirks

Platform behaviour learned the hard way, with citations — including disproofs of anything in
`AGENTS.md`, `agents/rules/**` or `students.md` (R5: record the disproof, name the file and
line it corrects).

- **CI is label- and path-gated.** A docs/Markdown-only PR runs no checks and `required` still
  passes; without `ready-for-e2e` no build or e2e job runs at all — `.github/workflows/pr.yml`,
  verified 2026-09-14.
- **`yarn test` does not run the timezone project.** CI runs the suite a second time with
  `VITEST_MODE=timezone`; the selection happens at `vitest.workspace.ts:7` — verified
  2026-09-14.
- **Next.js is 16.2.3, not 14.** `apps/web/package.json` `dependencies.next` = `16.2.3`,
  verified 2026-09-14. This **disproves** `students.md` ("Next.js 14", with a link to the
  Next 14 docs) and `AGENTS.md` §Tech Stack ("Next.js 13+"). Both are stale; neither is ours
  to edit (R13). Treat any framework-version claim in those two files as a lead only (R3).
- **API v2 is NestJS** — `apps/api/v2/package.json` depends on `@nestjs/common` et al.,
  verified 2026-09-14.
- **Correction: a database *is* possible here.** This file previously said no DB-backed work
  could run because Docker is absent. Homebrew has `postgresql@14` (14.18) installed with
  `postgres`, `pg_ctl` and `initdb` on PATH — it is simply not started, and nothing is listening
  on the `.env` default port 5450. So **D1 (run the app locally) is achievable** without Docker;
  it needs Postgres started, the `calendso` database created, migrations applied and a seed.
  Verified 2026-09-14.
- **`docs/sprint0/standards.md` is @lexzach's (Zachary Bowden), on his open WIP PR #7.** It is a
  shared team deliverable (D3, one per team), so changes belong there as review suggestions or
  Zulip coordination — **do not push to that branch**. A drafted Definition of Done plus the two
  conflict fixes are in `docs/agent/proposed-definition-of-done.md` (private, uncommitted).
- **The team's standards exist, unmerged, on PR #7.** `docs/sprint0/standards.md` on branch
  `docs/standards-guidelines` (opened 2026-09-13, still titled `WIP:`) covers branch names
  (`docs|feat|fix`/`name`), commit names (present tense, `Add …`), PR process, testing
  expectations, AI tool use and a **Definition of Done heading with no content**. It says
  nothing about AI-log links. Verified 2026-09-14 — and because it is `WIP:`, its own rule says
  it is not to be reviewed for merging, so **none of it binds yet**. Three conflicts with rules
  live on `main` are recorded in `docs/AGENT-PRACTICES.md` §Posture.
- **Branch `short` does not match the proposed branch convention** (`docs|feat|fix`/`name`).
  Harmless while PR #7 is unmerged, but a future branch should be e.g. `docs/agent-standard`.
- **The AI-log deliverable has a documented shape** (`ai-logs/README.md`, tracked, added in
  `02e09b9cb3`): `ai-logs/sprint<N>/<github-username>/YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-description>.md`,
  with a sibling directory of the same name for attachments; the tool id for this tool is
  `claude-code`. **But the instructions it defers to do not exist**: it links
  `docs/sprints.md#d4--ai-tooling-setup`, and `docs/sprints.md` is on no ref (verified
  2026-09-14, `git log --all --diff-filter=A -- docs/sprints.md`); the relative path in that
  link (`../../docs/`) also points above the repo root. **Correction to this file's earlier
  claim** that the repo documented no course conventions: it does, and the grep that "proved"
  otherwise searched for words the file does not contain (R4).
- **`yarn build` writes to your database. It is not read-only.** `packages/prisma`'s build
  script is `ts-node --transpile-only ./auto-migrations.ts`, and `auto-migrations.ts:34` runs
  **`yarn prisma migrate deploy`** against whatever `DATABASE_URL` is set to. `CONTRIBUTING.md`
  §Building tells every contributor to run `yarn build` before pushing, and says nothing about
  this. **Never run `yarn build` with `.env` pointed at a shared, staging or production
  database** — it will apply pending migrations to it.
- **`yarn build`'s "no database, skip gracefully" guard does not work.**
  `auto-migrations.ts` intends to skip when the DB is absent, but
  `is-prisma-available-check.ts` returns `false` only for `Prisma.PrismaClientInitializationError`
  and **rethrows every other error**. A refused connection to a Postgres that is not running is
  not that class, so it escapes the guard, reaches `main().catch()` and exits 1. Net effect on a
  machine with no Docker: the documented pre-push command **fails in 20s** at
  `@calcom/prisma#build` with ``Invalid `prisma.$queryRaw()` invocation``, and the failure looks
  like a code problem when it is an environment one. Escape hatch: `SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS=1`
  (`auto-migrations.ts:17`). Verified 2026-09-14.
- **A nested worktree doubles the test suite and turns it red — measured.** With a worktree at
  `.claude/worktrees/`, `TZ=UTC yarn test` from the primary checkout reported **830 files (208
  failed) / 6323 tests (38 failed), exit 1**. The identical tree with `--exclude '**/.claude/**'`
  reported **406 files (0 failed) / 4119 tests (0 failed), exit 0**. All 208 "failures" were
  duplicate copies, 202 of them `(0 test)` import errors because the nested checkout has source
  but no `node_modules`. `vitest list` also exits 1 in that state. Verified 2026-09-14.
  **Check `git worktree list` before trusting a test count.**
- **`CLAUDE.local.md` IS loaded by this harness.** Confirmed 2026-09-14: a session restart
  re-read instruction files and listed `/Users/zachshort/Projects/cal.diy/CLAUDE.local.md` as
  "user's private project instructions, not checked in". The private router works where it is;
  it does not need to move into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
- **`yarn lint` is turbo-cached and the documented command has no `--force`** — it can print
  `>>> FULL TURBO` having executed nothing. Use `yarn lint --force` when the number matters.
  See §Environment. Verified 2026-09-14.
- **Nested worktrees live inside the repo.** Claude Code puts them at
  `.claude/worktrees/<name>/`, i.e. *inside* `~/Projects/cal.diy`. Git ignores that path
  (`.git/info/exclude`), but tools that glob the filesystem do not necessarily. Test output on
  2026-09-14 showed vitest reporting files under `.claude/worktrees/.../apps/...` while running
  from the primary checkout. `type-check` and `lint` are **not** affected — turbo scopes them to
  the `workspaces` globs in `package.json` (`apps/*`, `packages/*`, ...), none of which match
  `.claude/worktrees/**`.
- **`turbo run type-check:ci` replays cached results**; `--force` is why `AGENTS.md` prescribes
  it.

### 4. Tell the team `yarn build` migrates the database

*Opened 2026-09-14, out of HANDOFF 4.* This is the one finding from setup that can cost someone
else real work, and it is invisible in the docs they are told to follow.

**Model: Default. Lane B. Waits on nothing.**

`CONTRIBUTING.md` §Building tells every contributor to run `yarn build` before pushing.
`packages/prisma`'s build script is `ts-node --transpile-only ./auto-migrations.ts`, and
`auto-migrations.ts:34` runs `yarn prisma migrate deploy` against `DATABASE_URL`. So a
classmate whose `.env` points at a shared or staging database will migrate it by following the
documented instructions. Separately, the intended "skip when there is no database" guard does
not work: `is-prisma-available-check.ts` returns `false` only for
`Prisma.PrismaClientInitializationError` and rethrows everything else, so a refused connection
escapes it and the build dies at `@calcom/prisma#build` with an error that reads like a code
problem.

Do these, in order:
1. **Reproduce both** on the current `main` before reporting anything (R3 — this was verified on

# Contributing to Cal.diy

> **Important:** Cal.diy is a community-driven, open-source fork of Cal.com. Contributions made here **do not** get merged into Cal.com's production service — Cal.com is now closed-source. This repo is maintained independently by the community under the MIT license.

Contributions are what make the open source community such an amazing place to learn, inspire, and create. Any contributions you make are **greatly appreciated**.

## House Rules (for PRs and Issues)

### 👥 Prevent Work Duplication

Before submitting a new issue or PR, check if it already exists in the [Issues](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/issues) or [Pull Requests](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/pulls).

### ✅ Work Only on Approved Issues

For feature requests, please wait for a core team member to approve and remove the `🚨 needs approval` label before you start coding or submitting a PR.

For bugs, security, performance, documentation, etc., you can start coding immediately—even if the `🚨 needs approval` label is present.

We highly value new feature ideas, but to maintain consistency in the product direction, they must go through a review and approval process.

### 🚫 Don’t Just Drop a Link

Avoid posting third-party links (e.g., Slack threads or Linear tickets) without context. A GitHub issue or PR should stand on its own—reviewers shouldn’t have to chase information across multiple tools to understand the context.

### 👀 Think Like a Reviewer

Put yourself in the reviewer’s shoes. What would you want to know if reading this for the first time? Are there key decisions, goals, or constraints that need clarification? Does the PR assume knowledge that isn’t obvious? Are there related issues or previous PRs that should be linked?

### 🧵 Bring in Context from Private Channels

If the task originated from a private conversation (e.g., Slack), take a moment to extract the relevant details and include them in the GitHub issue or PR. Avoid sharing sensitive information, but make sure important reasoning is captured.

> Example:  
> “A user requested feature X to solve problem Y. I considered approaches A, B, and C, but chose C for the following reasons…”

### 📚 Treat It Like Documentation

GitHub is a shared source of truth. Every issue and PR contributes to the long-term understanding of the codebase. Write clearly enough that someone—possibly you—can revisit it months later and still understand what happened and why.

### ✅ Summarize Your PR at the Top

Even if the code changes are minor or self-explanatory, a short written summary helps reviewers quickly understand the intent. You can use GitHub Copilot’s auto-summarize feature, but make sure to verify it for accuracy and relevance.

### 🔗 Use GitHub Keywords to Auto-Link Issues

Use phrases like “Closes #123” or “Fixes #456” in your PR descriptions. This automatically links your PR to the related issue and closes it once merged—keeping everything traceable and organized.

### 🧪 Mention What Was Tested (and How)

Explain how you validated your changes. It doesn’t need to be exhaustive—just enough to give reviewers confidence that things were tested and work as expected.

> Example:  
> “Tested locally with mock data and confirmed the flow works on staging.”

### 🧠 Assume Future-You Won’t Remember

Write with the future in mind. If there are trade-offs, edge cases, or temporary workarounds, document them clearly so they don’t get lost or misinterpreted later.

## File Naming Conventions

To ensure consistency and make files easy to fuzzy-find, we follow the naming conventions below for **services**, **repositories**, and other class-based files.

### Repository Files

- Repository class files must include the `Repository` suffix.
- If the repository is backed by a specific technology (e.g. Prisma), prefix the filename and class name with it.
- File name must match the exported class exactly (PascalCase).

**Pattern:**

`Prisma<Entity>Repository.ts`

**Examples:**

```ts
// File: PrismaAppRepository.ts
export class PrismaAppRepository { ... }

// File: PrismaMembershipRepository.ts
export class PrismaMembershipRepository { ... }
```

This avoids ambiguous filenames like app.ts and improves discoverability in editors.

### Service Files

- Service class files must include the Service suffix.
- File name should be in PascalCase, matching the exported class.
- Keep naming specific — avoid generic names like AppService.ts.

**Pattern:**

`<Entity>Service.ts`

**Examples:**

```ts
// File: MembershipService.ts
export class MembershipService { ... }

// File: HashedLinkService.ts
export class HashedLinkService { ... }
```

**Note:**

- New files must avoid dot-suffixes like .service.ts or .repository.ts; these will be migrated from the existing codebase progressively.
- We still reserve suffixes such as .test.ts, .spec.ts, and .types.ts for their respective use cases.

## Building

You can build the project with:

```bash
yarn build
```

Please ensure that you can make a full production build before pushing code.

## Testing

More info on how to add new tests coming soon.

### Running Tests

[See README](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy#e2e-testing)

#### Resolving Issues

##### E2E Test Browsers Not Installed

Run `npx playwright install` to download test browsers and resolve the error below when running `yarn test-e2e`:

```
Executable doesn't exist at /Users/alice/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium-1048/chrome-mac/Chromium.app/Contents/MacOS/Chromium
```

## Linting

To check the formatting of your code:

```sh
yarn lint
```

If you get errors, be sure to fix them before committing.

## Making a Pull Request

### Keep PRs Small and Focused

Large PRs are difficult to review and more prone to errors. We strongly encourage smaller, self-contained PRs:

- **Size limits**: Keep PRs under 500 lines of code changed and under 10 code files modified (excludes documentation, lock files, and auto-generated files)
- **Single responsibility**: Each PR should address one concern (one feature, one bug fix, or one refactor)
- **Split large changes**: If your task requires extensive changes, break it into multiple PRs that can be reviewed and merged independently

**How to split large changes:**
- Separate database/schema changes from application logic
- Split frontend and backend changes when possible
- Do preparatory refactoring in a separate PR before adding new features
- Create PRs in dependency order (infrastructure first, then features)

### PR Checklist

- Be sure to [check the "Allow edits from maintainers" option](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/allowing-changes-to-a-pull-request-branch-created-from-a-fork) when creating your PR. (This option isn't available if you're [contributing from a fork belonging to an organization](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/5634))
- If your PR refers to or fixes an issue, add `refs #XXX` or `fixes #XXX` to the PR description. Replace `XXX` with the respective issue number. See more about [linking a pull request to an issue](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue).
- Fill out the PR template accordingly.
- Review the [App Contribution Guidelines](./packages/app-store/CONTRIBUTING.md) when building integrations.
- Lastly, make sure to keep your branches updated (e.g., click the `Update branch` button on the GitHub PR page).

=== future-work ===
# Cancellation Reason Requirement Future Work

## Enhancements

## Nice to Have

=== design head ===
# Cancellation Reason Requirement Design

## Overview

Add a dropdown setting in Event Type Advanced settings that allows hosts to configure when cancellation reasons are required from hosts and/or attendees.

## Problem Statement

Currently, cancellation reasons are always optional. Hosts need the ability to require reasons for better tracking and accountability.

## User Stories

- As a host, I want to require cancellation reasons from attendees so that I understand why bookings are cancelled
- As a host, I want to require my team to provide cancellation reasons so that we have records of why bookings were cancelled
- As a host, I want to make cancellation reasons optional when they're not needed

## Technical Design

### Database Changes

Add new enum `CancellationReasonRequirement` with values:
- `MANDATORY_BOTH`
- `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`
- `MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY`
- `OPTIONAL_BOTH`

Add column `requiresCancellationReason` to EventType model with default `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`.

Location: `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` (near `disableCancelling`/`disableRescheduling`)

### API Changes

Update `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` to validate cancellation reason based on:
- Event type's `requiresCancellationReason` setting
- Who is cancelling (host vs attendee)

### UI Changes

**Event Type Settings**

=== auto-migrations ===
import dotEnv from "dotenv";
import { exec as execCb } from "node:child_process";
import { promisify } from "node:util";

import { isPrismaAvailableCheck } from "./is-prisma-available-check";

dotEnv.config({ path: "../../.env" });

const exec = promisify(execCb);

/**
 * TODO: re-write this when Prisma.io gets a programmatic migration API
 * Thanks to @olalonde for the idea.
 * @see https://github.com/prisma/prisma/issues/4703#issuecomment-1447354363
 */
async function main(): Promise<void> {
  if (process.env.SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS === "1") {
    console.info("SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS set, skipping migrations");
    return;
  }
  if (!process.env.DATABASE_URL) {
    console.info("No DATABASE_URL found, skipping migrations");
    return;
  }
  if (!process.env.DATABASE_DIRECT_URL) {
    console.info("No DATABASE_DIRECT_URL found, skipping migrations");
    return;
  }
  if (!(await isPrismaAvailableCheck())) {
    console.info("Prisma can't be initialized, skipping migrations");
    return;
  }
  // throws an error if migration fails
  const { stdout, stderr } = await exec("yarn prisma migrate deploy", {
    env: {
      ...process.env,
    },
  });
  console.log(stdout);
  console.error(stderr);
}

main().catch((e) => {
  console.error(e.stdout || e.stderr || e.message);
  process.exit(1);
});
=== is-prisma-available-check ===
import { Prisma } from "./client";

export async function isPrismaAvailableCheck(): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    const { prisma } = await import("./index");

    await prisma.$queryRaw<unknown[]>(Prisma.sql`SELECT 1`);
    await prisma.$disconnect();
    return true;
  } catch (e: unknown) {
    if (e instanceof Prisma.PrismaClientInitializationError) {
      return false;
    }
    throw e;
  }
}

## Candidate 1 — Require a reason when a booking is rescheduled

**Labels:** `type: feature`, `scope: medium` · teammate-equivalent: `enhancement`, `effort:medium`

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Event types can already force a **cancellation** reason: the `CancellationReasonRequirement`
enum (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:149`) with `MANDATORY_BOTH` / `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` /
`MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY` / `OPTIONAL_BOTH`, stored on
`EventType.requiresCancellationReason` (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:287`) and enforced in
`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:157-166`. Rescheduling has no equivalent.
A `rescheduleReason` is collected (`packages/lib/bookings/SystemField.ts:10`,
`apps/web/components/dialog/RescheduleDialog.tsx:23`) but is always optional — `grep -rn
"requiresRescheduleReason\|RescheduleReasonRequirement"` over the repo returns nothing. So a host
who needs accountability gets it for cancellations and silently loses it for reschedules, which
is the same disruption to the same attendee.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Mirror the cancellation setting for reschedules: a `RescheduleReasonRequirement` enum and a
`requiresRescheduleReason` column on `EventType`, a matching dropdown in Event Type → Advanced
next to the cancellation one, and validation on the reschedule path that rejects an empty reason
with the same shape of error as `handleCancelBooking.ts:161-166`.

### User story

As a host, I want to require a reason when someone reschedules one of my bookings, so that I
have the same record of why my calendar moved that I already have for cancellations.

### Rough scope

**Medium** — the whole pattern already exists end to end (enum, column, migration
`packages/prisma/migrations/20260115111819_add_cancellation_reason_require/`, settings dropdown,
validation, and unit tests in
`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking/test/handleCancelBooking.test.ts`), so this
is one migration plus a parallel copy of known-good code rather than a new design.

### Source

`specs/cancellation-reason-requirement/future-work.md` lists "Reschedule reason requirement
(same pattern, separate setting)" as work deliberately deferred from that feature.

## Candidate 2 — `yarn build` migrates whatever database `DATABASE_URL` points at

**Labels:** `type: bug`, `scope: small` · teammate-equivalent: `bug`, `effort:low`

### Issue Summary

`CONTRIBUTING.md` §Building tells every contributor to run `yarn build` before pushing and says
nothing about side effects. But `packages/prisma`'s build script is
`ts-node --transpile-only ./auto-migrations.ts`, and `packages/prisma/auto-migrations.ts:34` runs
**`yarn prisma migrate deploy`** against `DATABASE_URL`. Following the documented instruction
with `.env` pointed at a shared, staging or teammate's database applies pending migrations to it.

The intended "no database → skip" guard does not work.
`packages/prisma/is-prisma-available-check.ts:11` returns `false` only for
`Prisma.PrismaClientInitializationError` and **rethrows everything else** (`:14`). A refused TCP
connection to a Postgres that is not running is not that class, so it escapes the guard, reaches
`main().catch()` and exits 1 — and the failure reads like a code bug rather than a missing
service.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Have no Postgres listening on the port in `.env`.
2. Run `yarn build`.

### Actual Results

Exit 1 after ~20s at `@calcom/prisma#build` with ``Invalid `prisma.$queryRaw()` invocation``.
With a database present and reachable, the build instead **migrates it** without asking.

### Expected Results

`yarn build` should not write to a database, or `CONTRIBUTING.md` must say that it does. With no
database reachable the build should skip migrations and continue, which is what the guard was
written to do.

### Technical details

Measured 2026-09-14, macOS, Node 22.14.0, yarn 4.12.0: bare `yarn build` exits 1 in 20s;
`SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS=1 yarn build` (the escape hatch at `auto-migrations.ts:17`) exits 0 in 2m46s
across 13 turbo tasks — so the tree is sound and the migration step is the only blocker.

### Rough scope

**Small** — widen the `catch` in `is-prisma-available-check.ts` to treat connection failures as
"unavailable", and add one line to `CONTRIBUTING.md` §Building; both are a few lines with an
obvious unit test.

### Source

Hit while setting up the project locally for D1 on 2026-09-14; traced to the two files above.

---

## Candidate 4 — Waitlist for fully-booked time slots  *(ambitious)*

**Labels:** `type: feature`, `scope: xl` · teammate-equivalent: `enhancement`, `effort:high`

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

When every slot on a booking page is taken, the page is a dead end: it renders
`"no_available_slots": "No available slots"` (`packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json:2239`) or
`"all_booked_today": "All booked."` (`:735`) and the visitor leaves with nothing. The host never
learns that demand existed, and when someone cancels — which the product handles well — the freed
slot is only found by whoever happens to reload the page. There is no waitlist anywhere in the
codebase: `rg -ni "waitlist|waiting.list"` across the repo (excluding `node_modules` and lock
files) returns zero matches.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Let a visitor join a waitlist for a date or an exact slot instead of hitting the dead end. When a
booking is cancelled or rescheduled away, notify waitlisted people in order with a
time-limited claim link. Hosts get a per-event-type toggle, a cap, and a list of who is waiting.

### User story

As someone trying to book a fully-booked host, I want to join a waitlist for a time I need, so
that I am told when it frees up instead of having to keep checking the page.

### Rough scope

**XL** — it needs a new Prisma model and migration, a hook into the cancel/reschedule paths to
release slots, notification delivery, an expiring claim flow with a race between claimants, host
settings UI, attendee UI, and i18n; and it has to respect `seatsPerTimeSlot`
(`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:222`) rather than assuming one booking per slot.

### Source

Own use of the running app during D1 setup (2026-09-14): booked out the seeded `pro` user's
`/pro/30min` page and found the empty state offers nothing to do next.

## Candidate 5 — Restore the Insights dashboard this fork advertises but does not ship  *(ambitious)*

**Labels:** `type: feature`, `scope: xl` · teammate-equivalent: `enhancement`, `effort:high`

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

The instance still behaves as though Insights exists. Migration
`packages/prisma/migrations/20230329000000_add_insights_feature_flag/migration.sql` seeds a
`Feature` row `('insights', true, 'Enable insights for this instance', 'OPERATIONAL')` — enabled
by default — and the copy ships: `"insights": "Insights"`
(`packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json:2718`), `"insights_subtitle": "View booking insights
across your events"` (`:2855`), `"insights_no_data_found_for_filter"` (`:2720`), plus the
marketing images `apps/web/public/tips/insights.jpg` and
`apps/web/public/upgrade/full_insights.png`. But there is **no insights route** — nothing under
`apps/web/app` matches `*insights*` — and no insights package under `packages/`. A self-hoster
reading the flag list is told the feature is on and then cannot find it.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Build an Insights page for this fork: bookings created / completed / cancelled / no-show over a
date range, busiest times, most-booked event types, and — since the data is already there —
cancellation reasons (`Booking.cancellationReason`, `packages/prisma/schema.prisma:880`), filtered
by user and by team. Read-only, behind the existing `insights` feature flag, reusing
`packages/features/data-table` for the tables rather than inventing a grid.

### User story

As a host or team admin, I want a dashboard of my booking history, so that I can see which event
types actually get booked and when people cancel, without exporting anything.

### Rough scope

**XL** — aggregate queries over `Booking` that must not be O(n²) or unindexed
(`agents/rules/performance-avoid-quadratic.md`), a new repository + service + tRPC router obeying
the layering rules, a new route and charts, date/team filtering, i18n, and tests; the existing
i18n keys and feature flag give it a spec but none of the implementation.

### Source

Found while auditing which documented paths still resolve in this fork (2026-09-14): the
`insights` feature flag and its UI strings survived the `refactor: Cal.diy (#28903)` cleanup that
removed the code behind them.

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Event types can already force a **cancellation** reason. The `CancellationReasonRequirement` enum (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:149`) offers `MANDATORY_BOTH` / `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` / `MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY` / `OPTIONAL_BOTH`, it is stored on `EventType.requiresCancellationReason` (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:287`), and it is enforced in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:157-166`.

Rescheduling has no equivalent. A `rescheduleReason` is collected (`packages/lib/bookings/SystemField.ts:10`, `apps/web/components/dialog/RescheduleDialog.tsx:23`) but it is always optional — `rg -n "requiresRescheduleReason|RescheduleReasonRequirement"` over the repo returns nothing.

So a host who needs accountability gets it for cancellations and silently loses it for reschedules, even though a reschedule disrupts the same attendee and moves the same calendar. Hosts who run paid or high-demand event types are the ones who feel it.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Mirror the cancellation setting for reschedules:

- a `RescheduleReasonRequirement` enum and a `requiresRescheduleReason` column on `EventType`, with the same four values and the same default posture;
- a dropdown in Event Type → Advanced, sitting next to the cancellation one;
- validation on the reschedule path that rejects an empty reason, shaped like the check at `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:161-166`;
- the reason surfaced wherever the cancellation reason already is.

### User story

As a host, I want to require a reason when someone reschedules one of my bookings, so that I have the same record of why my calendar moved that I already have for cancellations.

### Rough scope

**Medium.** The whole pattern already exists end to end — enum, column, migration (`packages/prisma/migrations/20260115111819_add_cancellation_reason_require/`), settings dropdown, validation, and unit tests in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking/test/handleCancelBooking.test.ts` — so this is one migration plus a parallel copy of known-good code, not a new design.

### Issue Summary

`CONTRIBUTING.md` §Building tells every contributor to run `yarn build` before pushing, and says nothing about side effects. But `packages/prisma`'s build script is `ts-node --transpile-only ./auto-migrations.ts`, and `packages/prisma/auto-migrations.ts:34` runs **`yarn prisma migrate deploy`** against `DATABASE_URL`. Following the documented instruction with `.env` pointed at a shared, staging or teammate's database applies pending migrations to it, without asking.

Separately, the "no database, so skip" guard does not work. `packages/prisma/is-prisma-available-check.ts:11` returns `false` only for `Prisma.PrismaClientInitializationError` and **rethrows everything else** (`:14`). A refused TCP connection to a Postgres that is not running is not that class, so it escapes the guard, reaches `main().catch()` and exits 1 — and the failure reads like a code bug rather than a missing service.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Have no Postgres listening on the port in your `.env`.
2. Run `yarn build`.

### Actual Results

Exit 1 after about 20 seconds at `@calcom/prisma#build`, with ``Invalid `prisma.$queryRaw()` invocation``.

With a database present and reachable, the build instead **migrates it** silently.

### Expected Results

`yarn build` should not write to a database, or `CONTRIBUTING.md` §Building must say that it does. With no database reachable, the build should skip migrations and continue — which is exactly what the guard was written to do.

### Technical details

Measured 2026-09-14 on macOS, Node 22.14.0, yarn 4.12.0:

- bare `yarn build` — **exit 1 in 20s**;
- `SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS=1 yarn build` (the escape hatch at `packages/prisma/auto-migrations.ts:17`) — **exit 0 in 2m46s**, 13 turbo tasks.

So the tree itself is sound; the migration step is the only blocker.

### Rough scope

**Small.** Widen the `catch` in `is-prisma-available-check.ts` so connection failures count as "unavailable", and add one line to `CONTRIBUTING.md` §Building. Both are a few lines, and the guard change has an obvious unit test.

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

When every slot on a booking page is taken, the page is a dead end. It renders `"no_available_slots": "No available slots"` (`packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json:2239`) or `"all_booked_today": "All booked."` (`:735`), and the visitor leaves with nothing to do.

Two things are lost at that moment. The visitor has no way to signal that they wanted this host and this week, so they go and book elsewhere. And the host never learns that the demand existed — a fully-booked page and a page nobody visited look identical from the dashboard.

Meanwhile the product already handles the other half well: bookings get cancelled and rescheduled all the time, and those freed slots currently go to whoever happens to reload the page first.

There is no waitlist anywhere in the codebase — `rg -ni "waitlist|waiting.list"` across the repo, excluding `node_modules` and lock files, returns zero matches.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Let a visitor join a waitlist instead of hitting the dead end:

- on a fully-booked booking page, offer "join the waitlist" for a specific slot or for a date;
- when a booking is cancelled or rescheduled away, notify waitlisted people in order with a **time-limited claim link**, so a slot is not held forever by someone who has stopped watching;
- give hosts a per-event-type toggle, a cap on waitlist size, and a view of who is waiting;
- let people leave the waitlist from the notification.

This benefits both sides: attendees stop refreshing, and hosts convert cancellations into bookings instead of into gaps.

### User story

As someone trying to book a fully-booked host, I want to join a waitlist for the time I need, so that I am told when it frees up instead of having to keep checking the page.

### Rough scope

**XL.** It needs a new Prisma model and migration, a hook into the cancel and reschedule paths to detect a released slot, notification delivery, an expiring claim flow that has to resolve a race between claimants, host settings UI, attendee UI, and i18n — and it must respect `EventType.seatsPerTimeSlot` (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:222`) rather than assuming one booking per slot.

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

# Node 26 (the machine default) breaks `prisma generate`: the zod generator calls
# fs.rmdir(..., {recursive:true}), removed in modern Node, and the whole command exits 1.
# Every command below goes through Node 22, so no command in this script can hit that.
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/node@22/bin:/opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@14/bin:$PATH"

# name:one-line description — single source of truth for both the menu and completion
COMMANDS=(
  "dev:Run the web app at localhost:3000"
  "db:Start Postgres and make sure the calendso database exists"
  "migrate:Apply pending Prisma migrations"
  "seed:Reseed the database (test users free:free and pro:pro)"
  "reset:Drop, recreate, migrate and reseed the database"
  "studio:Open Prisma Studio to browse the database"
  "types:Type-check everything (forced — turbo caches a stale green otherwise)"
  "lint:Lint everything (forced — a bare run can report FULL TURBO having checked nothing)"
  "test:Run the unit suite, excluding any nested worktree"
  "tz:Run the timezone test project, which the plain test run skips"
  "build:Production build, without touching the database"
  "gates:Run every gate, in the order CI runs them"
  "log:Save this project's AI session transcripts into ai-logs/sprint0/"
  "psql:Open a psql shell on the calendso database"
  "shell:Print the ~/.zshrc snippet for the cal function + completion"
  "help:List commands"
)

DB_URL="postgresql://zachshort@localhost:5432/calendso"

cmd_dev() {
  cmd_db
  yarn dev
}

cmd_db() {
  # Postgres is a brew service rather than Docker here; students.md assumes Docker, which
  # is not installed on this machine. `brew services start` is idempotent.
  brew services start postgresql@14 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  for _ in $(seq 1 20); do nc -z localhost 5432 >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 0.5; done
  psql -p 5432 -d postgres -tAc "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='calendso'" | grep -q 1 \
    || createdb -p 5432 calendso
}

cmd_migrate() {
  cmd_db
  yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-migrate
}

cmd_seed() {
  cmd_db
  yarn db-seed
}

cmd_reset() {
  cmd_db
  dropdb -p 5432 --if-exists calendso
=== cmd_log ===
cmd_log() {
  # SpecStory buckets sessions by the directory the agent ran in, so a session started in
  # .claude/worktrees/<name>/ is invisible from the repo root and looks like it never
  # happened. Sync from each directory that has sessions, not just this one.
  local stage; stage="$(mktemp -d)"
  local out="$ROOT/ai-logs/sprint0/zach-short"
  mkdir -p "$out"
  specstory sync --output-dir "$stage" --local-time-zone --no-cloud-sync >/dev/null
  for wt in "$ROOT"/.claude/worktrees/*/; do
    [[ -d "$wt" ]] || continue
    (cd "$wt" && specstory sync --output-dir "$stage" --local-time-zone --no-cloud-sync >/dev/null) || true
  done

  shopt -s nullglob
  for f in "$stage"/*.md; do
    # Claude Code fires its own internal sessions — the editor-tab namer is one — which are
    # not development work and would pad the deliverable with noise.
    if head -20 "$f" | grep -q 'You maintain a 2-3 word tag'; then
      echo "skipped (internal tab-namer): $(basename "$f")"
      continue
    fi
    # SpecStory names files <date>_<time>-<slug>.md; the course requires
    # <date>_<tool>_<slug>.md (https://csci-435-se.github.io/ai-logs/).
    local base date slug
    base="$(basename "$f" .md)"
    date="${base%%_*}"
    slug="$(echo "${base#*_}" | sed -E 's/^[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{4}-//')"
    cp "$f" "$out/${date}_claude-code_${slug}.md"
    echo "wrote ${date}_claude-code_${slug}.md"
  done
  shopt -u nullglob
  rm -rf "$stage"
  # SpecStory drops .project.json / statistics.json beside its output. They are tooling
  # metadata, not logs, and a dotfile is easy to miss with plain `ls`.
  rm -f "$out/.project.json" "$out/statistics.json"

  # Transcripts go in a repo. Read them before committing: SpecStory redacts by default,
  # but "by default" is not "verified".
  echo
  echo "Now scan for secrets before committing:"
  echo "  grep -rnE 'ghp_|github_pat_|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|AKIA|BEGIN .*PRIVATE KEY' $out"
}
```
</details></tool-use>
